title: Bird motif
subtitle: A flat applique robin-style bird with a breast panel and tail, 9 cm
excerpt: The bird motif builds a teardrop-shaped body in dc rows, a small triangle beak worked into the narrow end, a contrast colour breast panel, and a split tail of three chain loops at the wide end. At 9 cm long in DK cotton it works as an applique on cushion covers, blankets, and children's garments.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from flat applique bird construction. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 9 (1894), flat applied bird motif chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A crochet bird applique in dark blue DK cotton with an orange breast panel and beak, three chain tail loops, photographed flat on natural linen in soft daylight. 9 cm long, clearly a perching bird.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished bird motif measures 9 cm long and 5 cm tall at the widest point in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Bird motif
chartDefinition.caption: Flat teardrop body in rows: chain foundation, increase rows to widest point, decrease rows to tail end. Beak: small triangle from the head end. Tail: three chain loops from the tail end.

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat shape that is wide at one end and narrows to a point at the other. Worked by increasing stitches from a narrow foundation, then decreasing back down.

content.text: worked in short rows: a chain foundation at the head end, increase rows to the widest point at the breast, then decrease rows toward the tail. A small triangle beak is worked in contrast colour from the narrow head end. Three chain loops form the split tail. A breast panel in a second colour is worked in the same stitch as the body but over a smaller row span, then sewn in place.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g of main body DK cotton, 3 g of contrast breast colour, 2 g of beak colour. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Embroidery thread for the eye. Scissors.

content.text: Each finished bird motif measures 9 cm long and 5 cm tall at the widest point in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
half treble (htr) — UK; US "half double crochet".

Ch 14. Dc in 2nd ch from hook and across. (12 dc.) Turn. Row 2: Ch 1. 2dc in first dc. Dc to last dc. 2dc in last dc. (14 dc.) Turn. Row 3: Ch 1. 2dc. Dc across to last. 2dc. (16 dc.) Turn. Row 4: Ch 1. Dc across evenly. (16 dc.) Turn. Row 5: Ch 1. Dc2tog. Dc across to last 2. Dc2tog. (14 dc.) Turn. Row 6: Ch 1. Dc2tog. Dc across to last 2. Dc2tog. (12 dc.) Turn. Row 7: Ch 1. Dc2tog. Dc across to last 2. Dc2tog. (10 dc.) Fasten off.
Join contrast colour at the centre of the head end (the narrow end, row 1 edge). Dc into first st. Htr into next st. Dc into next st. Sl st to anchor. Fasten off. This forms a small pointed beak.

Join main colour at the tail end (the wide end, row 7). Work three tail loops: *sl st into the edge st. Ch 6. Sl st back into the same st.* Repeat twice more, spacing the loops along the tail edge. Fasten off.

Ch 8. Dc in 2nd ch from hook and across. (6 dc.) Turn. Work 2 more rows even. Fasten off. Sew the breast panel onto the lower centre of the body with a tapestry needle, covering rows 3 to 5 of the body.

definition.title: Bird motif
definition.caption: 7-row teardrop body: inc in rows 2-3, even in row 4, dec in rows 5-7. Beak from head end. Tail loops from wide end.

content.text: Embroider a small French knot eye near the head end. Sew the assembled bird onto the base fabric through the body perimeter.
Handwash with the base fabric in cool water. Lay flat to dry.

The butterfly motif (crochet-animal-butterfly) builds on the same flat-row construction with four wing panels instead of a body. The fish motif (crochet-animal-fish) uses a similar teardrop with a fan tail instead of loop tail.
